key_insight: RareDx improves rare-disease diagnosis by combining controlled knowledge use with graph-grounded policy optimization so the model ranks valid disease candidates instead of hallucinating common or plausible-but-wrong names.
engineering_relevance: The paper shows that structured retrieval, ontology-aware rewards, and routing constraints can make a compact language model a stronger diagnostic ranker across heterogeneous clinical knowledge sources.
method: RareDx-Harness normalizes records into a shared ranked-diagnosis benchmark across direct inference, retrieval, tools, and phenotype-gene-disease reasoning.
RareDx-KGPO trains with rewards from canonical disease-graph projection, curated relevance, ontology proximity, biomedical similarity, and phenotype consistency.
Vocabulary and output-budget constraints reduce fabricated or overly long differential diagnoses during training.
evidence_signal: Across eight benchmarks, the Qwen3.5-9B-based system reached 38.34 macro Hit@10, outperforming GPT-5.5 by 1.60 points under the archived protocol, with a disjoint audit showing a 6.80-point routing gain over Direct on held-out cases.
watch_item: Performance depends on careful routing and reward design, and the abstract notes that retrieval is not uniformly helpful, so deployment will require strong control of tool use and canonicalization.
paper_title: RareDx: Controlled Knowledge Integration and Graph-Grounded Policy Optimization for Rare-Disease Diagnosis
